narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 58.7% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—slightly more likely to fail than pass. This is a risk estimate, not a final judgment of your ability, but it was enough to deny admission. The strongest factor was your third-year class-rank decile: you were in the second decile, far below the accepted-student average near the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. The next most influential factor was your first-year class-rank decile: you were in the first decile, again well below the accepted average near the sixth decile, and it also pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score of 36, compared with an accepted average of about 37.18, was the third most influential factor, but in your case it contributed modestly toward passing rather than failure. To improve a future application, ask the admissions office for specific feedback, focus on strengthening or explaining your academic record—especially your early class ranks—consider retaking the LSAT if you can raise your score, and gather evidence of bar-exam readiness. Reapply when you can show a stronger, more consistent academic trajectory.
